197:     /// PTDLO: `'LineStyleOrder'` name-value whose value is a cell array with
198:     /// more than one style string.
199:     pub(crate) fn check_ptdlo(&self, node: Node, source: &str, diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>) {
200:         for (arg, _) in named_args(node) {
201:             if arg_text(arg, source) != Some("LineStyleOrder") {
202:                 continue;
203:             }
204:             // The value is the next named argument (works for both
205:             // `'LineStyleOrder', {...}` and `LineStyleOrder={...}` forms).
206:             if let Some(value) = arg.next_named_sibling() {
207:                 if cell_style_count(value, source) >= 2 {
208:                     fire(arg, "PTDLO", MSG_PTDLO, diagnostics);
209:                 }
210:             }
211:         }
212:     }
213: }

219: /// The callee name of a `function_call` node, if any.
220: fn call_name<'a>(call: Node<'a>, source: &'a str) -> Option<&'a str> {
221:     let name = call.child_by_field_name("name")?;
222:     Some(&source[name.start_byte()..name.end_byte()])
223: }
224: 
225: /// Named children of a call's argument list, paired with a flag that is true
226: /// for positional arguments (those carrying the `argument:` field). `Name =
227: /// value` names/values are unnamed and get `false`.
228: fn named_args<'a>(call: Node<'a>) -> Vec<(Node<'a>, bool)> {
229:     let mut result = Vec::new();
230:     let mut cursor = call.walk();
231:     let args = call
232:         .children(&mut cursor)
233:         .find(|child| child.kind() == "arguments");
234:     let Some(args) = args else {
235:         return result;
236:     };
237:     let mut args_cursor = args.walk();
238:     for (index, child) in args.children(&mut args_cursor).enumerate() {
239:         if child.is_named() {
240:             let is_positional = args.field_name_for_child(index as u32) == Some("argument");
241:             result.push((child, is_positional));
242:         }
243:     }
244:     result
245: }
246: 
247: /// The string/identifier text of an argument, with surrounding quotes removed
248: /// for string literals.
249: fn arg_text<'a>(arg: Node<'a>, source: &'a str) -> Option<&'a str> {
250:     match arg.kind() {
251:         "string" => Some(unquoted(arg, source)),
252:         "identifier" => Some(&source[arg.start_byte()..arg.end_byte()]),
253:         _ => None,
254:     }
255: }
256: 
257: /// Strip the surrounding quotes from a string-literal node's text.
258: fn unquoted<'a>(node: Node<'a>, source: &'a str) -> &'a str {
259:     let text = &source[node.start_byte()..node.end_byte()];
260:     let bytes = text.as_bytes();
261:     if bytes.len() >= 2
262:         && ((bytes[0] == b'\'' && bytes[bytes.len() - 1] == b'\'')
263:             || (bytes[0] == b'"' && bytes[bytes.len() - 1] == b'"'))
264:     {
265:         &text[1..text.len() - 1]
266:     } else {
267:         text
268:     }
269: }
270: 
271: /// True when the callee is `set`, `get`, or `feature`.
272: fn is_set_get_or_feature(func_name: Option<&str>) -> bool {
273:     matches!(func_name, Some("set") | Some("get") | Some("feature"))
274: }
275: 
276: /// True when the argument is used as the *name* of a name-value pair: either a
277: /// `Name = value` identifier (immediately followed by `=`), or a positional
278: /// argument that is followed by another argument (its value).
279: fn is_name_value_name(arg: Node, is_positional: bool, index: usize, total: usize) -> bool {
280:     if arg.kind() == "identifier" {
281:         arg.next_sibling()
282:             .is_some_and(|sibling| sibling.kind() == "=")
283:     } else {
284:         is_positional && index + 1 < total
285:     }
286: }
287: 
288: /// True when a removed property/setting name appears in a name context: as an
289: /// argument to `set`/`get`/`feature`, or as the name of a name-value pair.
290: fn in_name_context(
291:     func_name: Option<&str>,
292:     arg: Node,
293:     is_positional: bool,
294:     index: usize,
295:     total: usize,
296: ) -> bool {
297:     if is_set_get_or_feature(func_name) && arg.kind() == "string" {
298:         return true;
299:     }
300:     is_name_value_name(arg, is_positional, index, total)
301: }
302: 
303: /// True when the callee is a function PTCLO applies to.
304: fn is_ptclo_func(func_name: Option<&str>) -> bool {
305:     match func_name {
306:         Some(name) => PTCLO_FUNCS.contains(&name),
307:         None => false,
308:     }
309: }
310: 
311: /// Number of non-empty string literals inside a cell array (PTDLO).
312: fn cell_style_count(value: Node, source: &str) -> usize {
313:     if value.kind() != "cell" {
314:         return 0;
315:     }
316:     let mut count = 0;
317:     let mut cursor = value.walk();
318:     for child in value.children(&mut cursor) {
319:         count += count_strings(child, source);
320:     }
321:     count
322: }
323: 
324: /// Count non-empty string literals under `node`, recursing through containers
325: /// (e.g. the `row` child of a cell).
326: fn count_strings(node: Node, source: &str) -> usize {
327:     if node.kind() == "string" {
328:         return if unquoted(node, source).is_empty() {
329:             0
330:         } else {
331:             1
332:         };
333:     }
334:     let mut count = 0;
335:     let mut cursor = node.walk();
336:     for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
337:         count += count_strings(child, source);
338:     }
339:     count
340: }
341: 
342: /// Scan one call for the given property/setting name and emit the check when
343: /// the name appears in a name context. Fires on the name node itself.
344: fn scan_name_args(
345:     call: Node,
346:     source: &str,
347:     property_name: &str,
348:     rule_id: &'static str,
349:     message: &'static str,
350:     diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
351: ) {
352:     let func_name = call_name(call, source);
353:     let args = named_args(call);
354:     let total = args.len();
355:     for (index, (arg, is_positional)) in args.iter().enumerate() {
356:         let Some(text) = arg_text(*arg, source) else {
357:             continue;
358:         };
359:         if text == property_name && in_name_context(func_name, *arg, *is_positional, index, total) {
360:             fire(*arg, rule_id, message, diagnostics);
361:         }
362:     }
363: }
364: 
365: /// Emit a warning diagnostic on the given node.
366: fn fire(
367:     node: Node,
368:     rule_id: &'static str,
369:     message: &'static str,
370:     diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
371: ) {
372:     let start = node.start_position();
373:     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
374:         rule_id,
375:         message: message.to_string(),
376:         severity: Severity::Warning,
377:         byte_range: node.start_byte()..node.end_byte(),
378:         line: start.row + 1,
379:         column: start.column + 1,
380:         fix: None,
381:     });
382: }

1: //! # Phase 7: Unset-variable and shared-variable compatibility checks
2: //!
3: //! Three behavior-change checks that MATLAB now enforces more strictly than in
4: //! previous releases. All three are file-level: they build a [`SymbolTable`]
5: //! over the whole tree and compare definition/use offsets within scopes.
6: //!
7: //! - **IDISVARLOW** — a name is indexed (`x(i)`, `x{i}`, `x.field`) before it
8: //!   is defined in the enclosing scope, so it could be mistaken for a function
9: //!   on the path. Fires on the indexing use. Only fires when the name is a
10: //!   genuine variable in that scope (defined somewhere in it): a name used
11: //!   only as a callee (`plot(x, y)`) is treated as a function and skipped, as
12: //!   are dotted/qualified calls (`pkg.func(x)`), file-defined functions, and
13: //!   builtin names.
14: //! - **IDISVARHIGH** — a plain read of a name with no prior definition in
15: //!   scope. Fires on the first such read. Callee/indexing uses are excluded
16: //!   (they belong to IDISVARLOW).
17: //! - **SHVAI** — a nested function reads/writes a name that the parent function
18: //!   also references, but the parent only defines it *after* the nested
19: //!   function's definition, so the shared variable is not initialized before
20: //!   the nested function can be called. Fires on the first offending parent
21: //!   definition.
22: //!
23: //! The checks are deliberately narrow: only clear use-before-definition
24: //! patterns fire. Branch-partial cases are left to the `unset_variables`
25: //! engine (NODEF/USENS/PSET).
26: 
27: use super::super::CompatibilityEngine;
28: use mlt_core::{Diagnostic, Severity};
29: use std::collections::{HashMap, HashSet};
30: use tree_sitter::{Node, Tree};
31: 
32: use crate::analysis::symbols::{DefKind, Scope, ScopeKind, SymbolTable, VarDef, VarUse};
33: 
34: /// IDISVARLOW: indexing an undefined variable may resolve to a path function.
35: const IDISVARLOW_MSG: &str = "To avoid a potential conflict with functions on the path, explicitly define the variable before indexing into it.";
36: 
37: /// IDISVARHIGH: a variable must be explicitly defined before its first use.
38: const IDISVARHIGH_MSG: &str = "Variable must be explicitly defined before first use. In some cases, the definition was not required in previous releases, but it is now required.";
39: 
40: /// SHVAI: shared variables must be initialized before the nested function runs.
41: const SHVAI_MSG: &str = "Explicitly define shared variables in the parent function before calling the nested function. MATLAB does not share uninitialized variables between a nested function and the parent function.";
42: 
43: /// Names that are always defined by MATLAB and never need a user definition.
44: const BUILTINS: &[&str] = &[
45:     "true",
46:     "false",
47:     "pi",
48:     "inf",
49:     "Inf",
50:     "nan",
51:     "NaN",
52:     "eps",
53:     "i",
54:     "j",
55:     "end",
56:     "nargin",
57:     "nargout",
58:     "varargin",
59:     "varargout",
60:     "ans",
61: ];
62: 
63: /// How an identifier use is classified for the unset-variable checks.
64: ///
65: /// The symbol table records every identifier it treats as a usage, but the
66: /// checks only fire on some of those positions:
67: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
68: enum UseClass {
69:     /// Callee of a plain `function_call` (`x(i)`, `x{i}`) — ambiguous
70:     /// indexing/call context (IDISVARLOW's domain).
71:     CallName,
72:     /// Object of a plain `field_expression` (`x.field`) — indexing context.
73:     FieldObject,
74:     /// Callee name of a dotted call (`pkg.func(x)`): definitely a function or
75:     /// method call, never variable indexing. Skipped by both checks.
76:     QualifiedCallee,
77:     /// Object/qualifier of a dotted call (`dsp` in `dsp.FIRFilter(x)`):
78:     /// a package or namespace qualifier, not a variable read.
79:     QualifiedObject,
80:     /// Any other read (RHS, call argument, operator operand, ...).
81:     Plain,
82: }
83: 
84: /// File-level entry point: run all three unset/shared-variable checks.
85: pub(crate) fn collect_file_checks(
86:     engine: &CompatibilityEngine,
87:     tree: &Tree,
88:     source: &str,
89:     diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
90: ) {
91:     let symbol_table = SymbolTable::build(tree, source);
92:     let use_classes = classify_identifier_uses(tree.root_node());
93:     let known_functions = collect_known_functions(tree.root_node(), source);
94: 
95:     engine.check_idisvar_low(&symbol_table, &use_classes, &known_functions, diagnostics);
96:     engine.check_idisvar_high(&symbol_table, &use_classes, &known_functions, diagnostics);
97:     engine.check_shvai(&symbol_table, diagnostics);
98: }
99: 
100: impl CompatibilityEngine {
101:     /// IDISVARLOW: a variable is indexed before it is defined in its scope.
102:     fn check_idisvar_low(
103:         &self,
104:         symbol_table: &SymbolTable,
105:         use_classes: &HashMap<usize, UseClass>,
106:         known_functions: &HashSet<String>,
107:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
108:     ) {
109:         for scope in &symbol_table.scopes {
110:             for name in scope.used_names() {
111:                 if is_builtin(name) || known_functions.contains(name) {
112:                     continue;
113:                 }
114:                 // Only a genuine variable can conflict with a path function. A
115:                 // name with no definition in this scope (e.g. `plot(x, y)`) is
116:                 // treated as a function call, not an indexing conflict.
117:                 if !has_variable_def(scope, name) {
118:                     continue;
119:                 }
120:                 for use_ in uses_in_order(scope, name) {
121:                     if !matches!(
122:                         use_classes.get(&use_.byte_range.start),
123:                         Some(UseClass::CallName | UseClass::FieldObject)
124:                     ) {
125:                         continue;
126:                     }
127:                     if !has_def_before_or_at(scope, name, use_.byte_range.start) {
128:                         push_use_diag(
129:                             "IDISVARLOW",
130:                             IDISVARLOW_MSG,
131:                             use_,
132:                             Severity::Warning,
133:                             diagnostics,
134:                         );
135:                         break;
136:                     }
137:                 }
138:             }
139:         }
140:     }
141: 
142:     /// IDISVARHIGH: a plain read with no prior definition in scope.
143:     fn check_idisvar_high(
144:         &self,
145:         symbol_table: &SymbolTable,
146:         use_classes: &HashMap<usize, UseClass>,
147:         known_functions: &HashSet<String>,
148:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
149:     ) {
150:         for (scope_idx, scope) in symbol_table.scopes.iter().enumerate() {
151:             for name in scope.used_names() {
152:                 if is_builtin(name) || known_functions.contains(name) {
153:                     continue;
154:                 }
155:                 for use_ in uses_in_order(scope, name) {
156:                     // Indexing/call positions are IDISVARLOW's domain.
157:                     if !matches!(
158:                         use_classes.get(&use_.byte_range.start),
159:                         None | Some(UseClass::Plain)
160:                     ) {
161:                         continue;
162:                     }
163:                     if !has_def_before_or_at(scope, name, use_.byte_range.start)
164:                         && !has_def_in_ancestors(symbol_table, scope_idx, name)
165:                     {
166:                         push_use_diag(
167:                             "IDISVARHIGH",
168:                             IDISVARHIGH_MSG,
169:                             use_,
170:                             Severity::Warning,
171:                             diagnostics,
172:                         );
173:                         break;
174:                     }
175:                 }
176:             }
177:         }
178:     }
179: 
180:     /// SHVAI: a shared variable is only defined after the nested function.
181:     fn check_shvai(&self, symbol_table: &SymbolTable, diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>) {
182:         for scope in &symbol_table.scopes {
183:             if scope.kind != ScopeKind::NestedFunction {
184:                 continue;
185:             }
186:             let Some(parent_idx) = scope.parent else {
187:                 continue;
188:             };
189:             let parent = &symbol_table.scopes[parent_idx];
190:             let nested_start = scope.byte_range.start;
191: 
192:             let mut names: HashSet<&str> = HashSet::new();
193:             names.extend(scope.uses.iter().map(|u| u.name.as_str()));
194:             names.extend(scope.defs.iter().map(|d| d.name.as_str()));
195: 
196:             for name in names {
197:                 if is_builtin(name) {
198:                     continue;
199:                 }
200:                 // Only "variable" definitions count — a sibling nested
201:                 // function name is not a shared variable.
202:                 let parent_defs = parent.defs_of(name);
203:                 if parent_defs.is_empty() {
204:                     continue;
205:                 }
206:                 let variable_defs: Vec<&VarDef> = parent_defs
207:                     .into_iter()
208:                     .filter(|d| d.kind != DefKind::NestedFunction)
209:                     .collect();
210:                 if variable_defs.is_empty() {
211:                     continue;
212:                 }
213:                 // All definitions must occur after the nested function starts.
214:                 if variable_defs
215:                     .iter()
216:                     .all(|d| d.byte_range.start >= nested_start)
217:                 {
218:                     push_def_diag(
219:                         "SHVAI",
220:                         SHVAI_MSG,
221:                         variable_defs[0],
222:                         Severity::Warning,
223:                         diagnostics,
224:                     );
225:                 }
226:             }
227:         }
228:     }
229: }

231: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
232: // Helpers
233: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
234: 
235: /// True when the name is a MATLAB builtin that needs no user definition.
236: fn is_builtin(name: &str) -> bool {
237:     BUILTINS.contains(&name)
238: }
239: 
240: /// The uses of `name` in `scope`, ordered by byte offset.
241: fn uses_in_order<'a>(scope: &'a Scope, name: &str) -> Vec<&'a VarUse> {
242:     let mut uses = scope.uses_of(name);
243:     uses.sort_by_key(|u| u.byte_range.start);
244:     uses
245: }
246: 
247: /// True when `scope` defines `name` as a variable (any definition kind other
248: /// than a nested-function name).
249: fn has_variable_def(scope: &Scope, name: &str) -> bool {
250:     scope
251:         .defs_of(name)
252:         .iter()
253:         .any(|d| d.kind != DefKind::NestedFunction)
254: }
255: 
256: /// True when `scope` defines `name` at or before the given use offset.
257: fn has_def_before_or_at(scope: &Scope, name: &str, use_start: usize) -> bool {
258:     scope
259:         .defs_of(name)
260:         .iter()
261:         .any(|d| d.byte_range.start <= use_start)
262: }
263: 
264: /// True when any ancestor scope (shared-workspace scopes such as nested
265: /// functions and lambdas) defines `name`. A nested function may legitimately
266: /// read a parent's variable, so an ancestor definition suppresses IDISVARHIGH
267: /// (the shared-variable case is handled by SHVAI).
268: fn has_def_in_ancestors(symbol_table: &SymbolTable, mut scope_idx: usize, name: &str) -> bool {
269:     while let Some(parent_idx) = symbol_table.scopes[scope_idx].parent {
270:         if symbol_table.scopes[parent_idx].is_defined(name) {
271:             return true;
272:         }
273:         scope_idx = parent_idx;
274:     }
275:     false
276: }

278: /// Classify every identifier in the tree by its use position.
279: fn classify_identifier_uses(root: Node) -> HashMap<usize, UseClass> {
280:     let mut classes = HashMap::new();
281:     let mut stack = vec![root];
282:     while let Some(node) = stack.pop() {
283:         if node.kind() == "identifier" {
284:             if let Some(class) = classify_identifier(node) {
285:                 classes.insert(node.start_byte(), class);
286:             }
287:         }
288:         let mut cursor = node.walk();
289:         for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
290:             stack.push(child);
291:         }
292:     }
293:     classes
294: }
295: 
296: /// Classify one identifier based on its parent context.
297: fn classify_identifier(node: Node) -> Option<UseClass> {
298:     let parent = node.parent()?;
299:     match parent.kind() {
300:         "function_call" => {
301:             let is_name = parent
302:                 .child_by_field_name("name")
303:                 .map(|n| n.id() == node.id())
304:                 .unwrap_or(false);
305:             if !is_name {
306:                 return Some(UseClass::Plain);
307:             }
308:             // A dotted call (`pkg.func(x)`) has the function_call as the field
309:             // child of a field_expression: the callee is definitely a function.
310:             match parent.parent().map(|g| g.kind()) {
311:                 Some("field_expression") => Some(UseClass::QualifiedCallee),
312:                 _ => Some(UseClass::CallName),
313:             }
314:         }
315:         "field_expression" => {
316:             let is_field = parent
317:                 .child_by_field_name("field")
318:                 .map(|f| f.id() == node.id())
319:                 .unwrap_or(false);
320:             if is_field {
321:                 // The field name of `x.field` is not a variable read.
322:                 return None;
323:             }
324:             // The object/qualifier position. A field whose value is a call
325:             // (`dsp.FIRFilter(x)`, `x.field(1)`) is a qualified call, so the
326:             // object identifiers are namespace qualifiers, not variable reads.
327:             let has_call_field = named_children(parent)
328:                 .iter()
329:                 .any(|c| c.kind() == "function_call");
330:             if has_call_field {
331:                 Some(UseClass::QualifiedObject)
332:             } else {
333:                 Some(UseClass::FieldObject)
334:             }
335:         }
336:         _ => Some(UseClass::Plain),
337:     }
338: }
339: 
340: /// The named children of a node.
341: fn named_children(node: Node) -> Vec<Node> {
342:     let mut children = Vec::new();
343:     let mut cursor = node.walk();
344:     for child in node.named_children(&mut cursor) {
345:         children.push(child);
346:     }
347:     children
348: }

350: /// Names of every function and class defined in the file.
351: fn collect_known_functions(root: Node, source: &str) -> HashSet<String> {
352:     let mut known = HashSet::new();
353:     let mut stack = vec![root];
354:     while let Some(node) = stack.pop() {
355:         if matches!(node.kind(), "function_definition" | "class_definition") {
356:             if let Some(name) = node.child_by_field_name("name") {
357:                 known.insert(source[name.start_byte()..name.end_byte()].to_string());
358:             }
359:         }
360:         let mut cursor = node.walk();
361:         for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
362:             stack.push(child);
363:         }
364:     }
365:     known
366: }

1: //! # SYNTAX_ERRORS_ENGINE: Parser-Level and Semantic Syntax Validation
2: //!
3: //! ```mlt
4: //! id = "SYNTAX_ERRORS_ENGINE"
5: //! title = "Syntax Errors"
6: //! category = "syntax-errors"
7: //! severity = "error"
8: //! fix = true
9: //! icon = "lucide/x-circle"
10: //! slug = "syntax-errors"
11: //! ```
12: //!
13: //! ## Rule
14: //!
15: //! Detects syntax errors in MATLAB source files. The engine combines
16: //! tree-sitter `ERROR`/`MISSING` node analysis with semantic checks the parser
17: //! cannot catch on its own: invalid operators, malformed file and function
18: //! names, structural violations, unterminated strings and comments, and
19: //! invalid numeric literals.
20: //!
21: //! A single file-level engine (`SyntaxErrorsEngine`) dispatches all 48 checks
22: //! in one pass over the parse tree, plus targeted source scans that skip over
23: //! comments and strings. Each diagnostic carries the specific check ID
24: //! (e.g. `SYNER`, `BADNE`, `SEPEXR`).
25: //!
26: //! ## Check IDs
27: //!
28: //! | Check ID | Severity | Fix | Description |
29: //! | --- | --- | --- | --- |
30: //! | SYNER | error | no | Parse error at VAR_RESERVED_WORD: usage might be invalid MATLAB syntax. |
31: //! | BDFIL | error | no | Invalid MATLAB file name. MATLAB file names must start with a letter, contain only letters, numbers, or underscores, and have no more than VAR_NUMBER characters. |
32: //! | BADNE | error | yes | 'Not Equals' is spelled ~= in MATLAB, not !=. |
33: //! | BADOT | error | no | Use of two dots (..) is an invalid MATLAB construction. |
34: //! | TWOCM | error | no | A comma cannot immediately follow another comma. |
35: //! | CLIS | error | no | Defining a class in script is not allowed. |
36: //! | CLTWO | error | no | Only one class definition is allowed per file, and it must come at the head of the file. |
37: //! | SOFOC | error | no | Statement outside a class definition is not allowed. |
38: //! | SEMFU | error | no | Script file must contain executable code. Remove empty statements to make this file a function file. |
39: //! | FNDOT | error | no | Function name can only contain dots if it is a class method. |
40: //! | FNSWA | error | no | Function name must start with alphabetic character. |
41: //! | NOPAR2 | error | no | A VAR_NAME might be missing a closing VAR_NAME, causing invalid syntax at VAR_NAME on line VAR_NUMBER. |
42: //! | EOLPAR | error | no | A VAR_NAME might be missing a closing VAR_NAME, causing invalid syntax at end of line. |
43: //! | ENDPAR | error | no | A VAR_NAME might be missing a closing VAR_NAME, causing invalid syntax at end of file. |
44: //! | ENDCT | error | no | An END might be missing, possibly matching VAR_RESERVED_WORD. |
45: //! | ENDCT2 | error | no | An END might be missing (after line VAR_RESERVED_WORD), possibly matching VAR_NUMBER. |
46: //! | ENDCT3 | error | no | An END might be missing (before VAR_RESERVED_WORD on line VAR_NUMBER), possibly matching VAR_RESERVED_WORD. |
47: //! | ENDCT4 | error | no | A METHODS block or END might be missing before the function definition. This might be causing additional error messages. |
48: //! | EOFMI | error | no | Invalid syntax at end of file. File is incomplete. |
49: //! | NOLHS | error | no | Left side of an assignment is empty. |
50: //! | BADCH | error | no | Invalid text character(s). |
51: //! | BADSP | error | no | Invalid text character(s). The text contains an unsupported non-ASCII whitespace character. |
52: //! | BADCT | error | no | Unicode explicit directional formatting characters are not supported. |
53: //! | REDEF | error | no | The current use of VAR_NAME is inconsistent with its previous use or definition (line VAR_NUMBER). |
54: //! | SEPEXR | error | yes | Use a newline, semicolon, or comma before this statement. |
55: //! | SBTMP | error | no | Invalid array indexing or function call. Chaining outputs after parenthesis is not supported. |
56: //! | FVSYN | error | no | Invalid function argument syntax at VAR_RESERVED_WORD. |
57: //! | FVACI | error | no | Use of name-value arguments in cell indexing is not supported. |
58: //! | FVACS | error | no | Using a character vector or string as a name in name=value syntax is not supported. Remove the quotes around the name. |
59: //! | FVAMI | error | no | Name in name-value argument syntax must be a valid MATLAB identifier. |
60: //! | UNSET | error | no | Invalid use of VAR_OPERATOR on the left side of an assignment. |
61: //! | LHROW | error | no | The left side of an assignment cannot have multiple rows (';'). |
62: //! | RESWD | error | no | Invalid use of a reserved word. |
63: //! | SYNEND | error | no | Invalid use for END operator. |
64: //! | MCPLD | error | no | Invalid property syntax at VAR_RESERVED_WORD. |
65: //! | BADNOT | error | no | Using ~ to ignore a value is not permitted in this context. |
66: //! | BADNOTLHS | error | no | Invalid use of logical not operator (~) on left side of an assignment. To use ~ to ignore function outputs, separate output variables with commas. |
67: //! | STRIN | error | no | A quoted character vector is unterminated. |
68: //! | DOUQT | error | no | A double quoted string is unterminated. |
69: //! | INBLK | error | no | A block comment is unterminated at the end of the file. |
70: //! | BADFP | error | no | Invalid floating-point constant. |
71: //! | BADHBH | error | no | Invalid digit in hexadecimal literal. Supported hexadecimal digits are 0-9 and A-F. Supported type suffixes are u8, u16, u32, u64, and s8, s16, s32, s64. |
72: //! | BADHBB | error | no | Invalid digit in binary literal. Supported binary digits are 0 and 1. Supported type suffixes are u8, u16, u32, u64, and s8, s16, s32, s64. |
73: //! | BADHBHT | error | no | Hexadecimal literal has too many digits for specified type suffix. |
74: //! | BADHBBT | error | no | Binary literal has too many digits for specified type suffix. |
75: //! | HEXTOOLONG | error | no | Hexadecimal literal has too many digits. |
76: //! | BINARYTOOLONG | error | no | Binary literal has too many digits. |
77: //! | VTPOD | error | no | Specify validation in the following order: size, then class, then functions. |
78: //!
79: //! ## Fix
80: //!
81: //! Two checks carry automatic fixes:
82: //!
83: //! - `BADNE` rewrites `!=` to `~=`, the MATLAB not-equal operator.
84: //! - `SEPEXR` inserts a `;` between two statements that share a line with no
85: //!   separator.
86: //!
87: //! ## Examples
88: //!
89: //! ### Incorrect
90: //!
91: //! ```matlab
92: //! x = 1 != 2;      % BADNE: `!=` is not MATLAB
93: //! a = 1 b = 2;     % SEPEXR: statements on one line without separator
94: //! if x > 0
95: //!     y = 'unterminated;   % STRIN
96: //! ```
97: //!
98: //! ### Correct
99: //!
100: //! ```matlab
101: //! x = 1 ~= 2;
102: //! a = 1; b = 2;
103: //! if x > 0
104: //!     y = 'terminated';
105: //! end
106: //! ```
107: //!
108: //! ### Fixed
109: //!
110: //! ```diff
111: //! - x = 1 != 2;
112: //! + x = 1 ~= 2;
113: //! - a = 1 b = 2;
114: //! + a = 1; b = 2;
115: //! ```
116: //!
117: //! ## Configuration
118: //!
119: //! ```toml
120: //! [lint.rules.SYNTAX_ERRORS_ENGINE]
121: //! disabled_checks = []
122: //! ```

217: /// Deserialized from the `[lint.rules.SYNTAX_ERRORS_ENGINE]` section in `.mlt.toml`.
218: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Deserialize, Default)]
219: pub struct SyntaxErrorsConfig {
220:     /// List of individual check IDs to disable (e.g., `["BADOT", "TWOCM"]`).
221:     #[serde(default)]
222:     pub disabled_checks: Vec<String>,
223: }

225: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
226: // Rule implementation
227: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
228: 
229: /// semantic syntax validation in a single pass.
230: pub struct SyntaxErrorsEngine {
231:     /// Set of disabled check IDs for fast lookup.
232:     disabled: HashSet<String>,
233: }
234: 
235: impl SyntaxErrorsEngine {
236:     /// Factory constructor. Reads rule-specific params from config.
237:     pub fn from_config(config: &Config) -> Box<dyn Rule> {
238:         let rule_config: SyntaxErrorsConfig = config.rule_params("SYNTAX_ERRORS_ENGINE");
239:         let disabled: HashSet<String> = rule_config.disabled_checks.into_iter().collect();
240:         Box::new(Self { disabled })
241:     }
242: 
243:     /// Returns true if the given check ID is enabled.
244:     fn is_check_enabled(&self, check_id: &str) -> bool {
245:         !self.disabled.contains(check_id)
246:     }
247: 
248:     // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
249:     // Source text scanning (BADNE, BADOT, TWOCM, BADCH, BADSP)
250:     // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
251: 
252:     /// source-level scanning.
253:     pub(crate) fn collect_skip_ranges(node: Node, ranges: &mut Vec<Range<usize>>) {
254:         if node.kind() == "comment" || node.kind() == "string" {
255:             ranges.push(node.byte_range());
256:             return;
257:         }
258:         let mut cursor = node.walk();
259:         for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
260:             Self::collect_skip_ranges(child, ranges);
261:         }
262:     }
263: 
264:     /// Check if a byte position is inside a skip range.
265:     pub(crate) fn in_skip_range(pos: usize, ranges: &[Range<usize>]) -> bool {
266:         ranges.iter().any(|r| r.contains(&pos))
267:     }
268: 
269:     // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
270:     // Tree ERROR/MISSING node analysis (SYNER, NOPAR2, EOLPAR, ENDPAR, ENDCT, EOFMI)
271:     // -----------------------------------------------------------------------
272: 
273:     /// Heuristic: does this error text look like an unclosed bracket?
274:     pub(crate) fn looks_like_missing_bracket(text: &str) -> bool {
275:         let opens: usize = text
276:             .chars()
277:             .filter(|&c| c == '(' || c == '[' || c == '{')
278:             .count();
279:         let closes: usize = text
280:             .chars()
281:             .filter(|&c| c == ')' || c == ']' || c == '}')
282:             .count();
283:         opens > closes
284:     }
285: 
286:     /// the given error text.
287:     pub(crate) fn bracket_kinds(text: &str) -> Vec<&str> {
288:         let mut kinds = Vec::new();
289:         for (open, close, kind) in [('(', ')', "("), ('[', ']', "["), ('{', '}', "{")] {
290:             let opens = text.chars().filter(|&c| c == open).count();
291:             let closes = text.chars().filter(|&c| c == close).count();
292:             if opens > closes {
293:                 kinds.push(kind);
294:             }
295:         }
296:         kinds
297:     }
298: 
299:     /// Returns the matching opener for a missing closing bracket kind.
300:     pub(crate) fn missing_bracket_opener(kind: &str) -> Option<&'static str> {
301:         match kind {
302:             ")" => Some("("),
303:             "]" => Some("["),
304:             "}" => Some("{"),
305:             _ => None,
306:         }
307:     }
308: 
309:     /// before end of file.
310:     pub(crate) fn is_end_of_file(node: Node, source: &str) -> bool {
311:         source[node.end_byte()..]
312:             .bytes()
313:             .all(|b| matches!(b, b'\n' | b'\r' | b' ' | b'\t' | b';' | b','))
314:     }
315: 
316:     /// whitespace, `;`, or `,` follow it up to the next newline).
317:     pub(crate) fn is_line_ending(node: Node, source: &str) -> bool {
318:         let rest = &source[node.end_byte()..];
319:         let line_end = rest.find('\n').unwrap_or(rest.len());
320:         rest[..line_end]
321:             .bytes()
322:             .all(|b| matches!(b, b'\r' | b' ' | b'\t' | b';' | b','))
323:     }
324: 
325:     /// Heuristic: does this error look like a missing `end`?
326:     pub(crate) fn looks_like_missing_end(text: &str, node: &Node) -> bool {
327:         // Check text for block openers without matching end.
328:         let lower = text.to_lowercase();
329:         let has_opener = BLOCK_OPENERS.iter().any(|kw| lower.contains(kw));
330:         let has_end = lower.contains("end");
331: 
332:         if has_opener && !has_end {
333:             return true;
334:         }
335: 
336:         // Check if previous sibling is a block statement.
337:         if let Some(prev) = node.prev_sibling() {
338:             let kind = prev.kind();
339:             if BLOCK_OPENERS.contains(&kind) {
340:                 return true;
341:             }
342:         }
343: 
344:         false
345:     }
346: 
347:     /// the call.
348:     pub(crate) fn is_in_function_call_args(node: &Node) -> bool {
349:         let mut current = node.parent();
350:         while let Some(ancestor) = current {
351:             match ancestor.kind() {
352:                 "arguments" => {
353:                     return ancestor
354:                         .parent()
355:                         .is_some_and(|p| p.kind() == "function_call");
356:                 }
357:                 "function_call" => {
358:                     // The ERROR is a direct child of the call. It is within the
359:                     // argument list when the call also has an `arguments` child.
360:                     let mut cursor = ancestor.walk();
361:                     return ancestor
362:                         .children(&mut cursor)
363:                         .any(|c| c.kind() == "arguments");
364:                 }
365:                 _ => {}
366:             }
367:             current = ancestor.parent();
368:         }
369:         false
370:     }
371: 
372:     /// that starts with a block-opening keyword).
373:     pub(crate) fn classify_missing_end(
374:         node: &Node,
375:         source: &str,
376:     ) -> Option<(&'static str, String)> {
377:         let start = node.start_byte();
378:         let node_end = node.end_byte().min(source.len());
379:         let text = &source[start..node_end];
380:         let lower = text.to_lowercase();
381:         let line = node.start_position().row + 1;
382: 
383:         // ENDCT4: ERROR text contains "classdef", a function_definition
384:         // follows it as a sibling, and no "methods" appears between them.
385:         if lower.contains("classdef") {
386:             let mut sibling = node.next_sibling();
387:             while let Some(sib) = sibling {
388:                 if sib.kind() == "function_definition" && sib.start_byte() > start {
389:                     let between = &source[node_end..sib.start_byte()];
390:                     if !between.to_lowercase().contains("methods") {
391:                         return Some((
392:                             "ENDCT4",
393:                             "A METHODS block or END might be missing before the function definition. This might be causing additional error messages.".to_string(),
394:                         ));
395:                     }
396:                     break;
397:                 }
398:                 sibling = sib.next_sibling();
399:             }
400:         }
401: 
402:         // ENDCT2: a block opener appears in the ERROR text or its previous
403:         // sibling, and the ERROR does not contain `end`.
404:         let has_end = lower.contains("end");
405:         if !has_end {
406:             let opener_in_text = BLOCK_OPENERS.iter().any(|kw| lower.contains(kw));
407:             let opener_in_prev = node
408:                 .prev_sibling()
409:                 .map(|prev| {
410:                     let prev_text = &source[prev.start_byte()..prev.end_byte()];
411:                     BLOCK_OPENERS
412:                         .iter()
413:                         .any(|kw| prev_text.to_lowercase().contains(kw))
414:                 })
415:                 .unwrap_or(false);
416:             if opener_in_text || opener_in_prev {
417:                 let raw_end = node.end_position().row;
418:                 let end_line = if source[..node_end].ends_with('\n') {
419:                     raw_end
420:                 } else {
421:                     raw_end + 1
422:                 };
423:                 let opener_line = if opener_in_text {
424:                     line
425:                 } else {
426:                     node.prev_sibling()
427:                         .map(|p| p.start_position().row + 1)
428:                         .unwrap_or(line)
429:                 };
430:                 return Some((
431:                     "ENDCT2",
432:                     format!(
433:                         "An END might be missing (after line {end_line}), possibly matching line {opener_line}."
434:                     ),
435:                 ));
436:             }
437:         }
438: 
439:         // ENDCT3: the ERROR is followed by a sibling that starts with a
440:         // block-opening keyword.
441:         let mut sibling = node.next_sibling();
442:         while let Some(sib) = sibling {
443:             let sib_text = &source[sib.start_byte()..sib.end_byte()];
444:             match sib_text.split_whitespace().next() {
445:                 Some(first) if BLOCK_OPENERS.contains(&first.to_lowercase().as_str()) => {
446:                     let kw = text.split_whitespace().next().unwrap_or("").to_uppercase();
447:                     let matched = first.to_uppercase();
448:                     return Some((
449:                         "ENDCT3",
450:                         format!(
451:                             "An END might be missing (before {kw} on line {line}), possibly matching {matched}."
452:                         ),
453:                     ));
454:                 }
455:                 Some(_) => break,
456:                 None => {}
457:             }
458:             sibling = sib.next_sibling();
459:         }
460: 
461:         None
462:     }

467:

470:     // -----------------------------------------------------------------------

484: 
485:     /// Returns the first reserved keyword appearing as a whole word in `text`.
486:     pub(crate) fn contains_reserved_word(text: &str) -> Option<&'static str> {
487:         let lower = text.to_lowercase();
488:         RESERVED_KEYWORDS
489:             .iter()
490:             .find(|&&kw| Self::contains_whole_word(&lower, kw))
491:             .copied()
492:     }
493: 
494:     /// Whole-word substring check: `needle` must not be part of a larger word.
495:     pub(crate) fn contains_whole_word(haystack: &str, needle: &str) -> bool {
496:         let mut search_start = 0;
497:         while let Some(rel) = haystack[search_start..].find(needle) {
498:             let idx = search_start + rel;
499:             let prev = haystack[..idx].chars().next_back();
500:             let next = haystack[idx + needle.len()..].chars().next();
501:             let left_ok = prev.is_none_or(|c| !c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() && c != '_');
502:             let right_ok = next.is_none_or(|c| !c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() && c != '_');
503:             if left_ok && right_ok {
504:                 return true;
505:             }
506:             search_start = idx + needle.len();
507:         }
508:         false
509:     }
510: 
511:     /// Returns true if `node` or any of its descendants has the given kind.
512:     pub(crate) fn has_descendant_kind(node: Node, kind: &str) -> bool {
513:         if node.kind() == kind {
514:             return true;
515:         }
516:         let mut cursor = node.walk();
517:         for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
518:             if Self::has_descendant_kind(child, kind) {
519:                 return true;
520:             }
521:         }
522:         false
523:     }

627:     pub(crate) fn parse_hex_binary_literal(text: &str) -> Option<(bool, usize, Option<&str>)> {
628:         let (is_hex, rest) = if text.starts_with("0x") || text.starts_with("0X") {
629:             (true, &text[2..])
630:         } else if text.starts_with("0b") || text.starts_with("0B") {
631:             (false, &text[2..])
632:         } else {
633:             return None;
634:         };
635: 
636:         if rest.is_empty() {
637:             return None;
638:         }
639: 
640:         let suffix = if rest.len() >= 3 && Self::suffix_bits(&rest[rest.len() - 3..]).is_some() {
641:             Some(&rest[rest.len() - 3..])
642:         } else if rest.len() >= 2 && Self::suffix_bits(&rest[rest.len() - 2..]).is_some() {
643:             Some(&rest[rest.len() - 2..])
644:         } else {
645:             None
646:         };
647: 
648:         let digits = match suffix {
649:             Some(s) => &rest[..rest.len() - s.len()],
650:             None => rest,
651:         };
652: 
653:         if digits.is_empty() {
654:             return None;
655:         }

657:         Some((is_hex, digits.chars().count(), suffix))

668:             return None;
669:         }
670:         match &suffix[1..] {
671:             "8" => Some(8),
672:             "16" => Some(16),
673:             "32" => Some(32),
674:             "64" => Some(64),
675:             _ => None,

188:                                     message: format!(
189:                                         "A {bracket} might be missing a closing {bracket}, causing invalid syntax at end of file."
190:                                     ),
191:                                     severity: Severity::Error,
192:                                     byte_range: start..end,
193:                                     line: pos.row + 1,
194:                                     column: pos.column + 1,
195:                                     fix: None,
196:                                 });
197:                         }
198:                     } else if Self::is_line_ending(node, source) {
199:                         if self.is_check_enabled("EOLPAR") {
200:                             diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
201:                                     rule_id: "EOLPAR",
202:                                     message: format!(
203:                                         "A {bracket} might be missing a closing {bracket}, causing invalid syntax at end of line."
204:                                     ),
205:                                     severity: Severity::Error,
206:                                     byte_range: start..end,
207:                                     line: pos.row + 1,
208:                                     column: pos.column + 1,
209:                                     fix: None,
210:                                 });
211:                         }
212:                     } else if self.is_check_enabled("NOPAR2") {
213:                         diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
214:                                 rule_id: "NOPAR2",
215:                                 message: format!(
216:                                     "A {bracket} might be missing a closing {bracket}, causing invalid syntax at {bracket} on line {}.",
217:                                     pos.row + 1
218:                                 ),
219:                                 severity: Severity::Error,
220:                                 byte_range: start..end,
221:                                 line: pos.row + 1,
222:                                 column: pos.column + 1,
223:                                 fix: None,
224:                             });
225:                     }
226:                 }
227:             } else if self.is_check_enabled("SYNER") {
228:                 let start = node.start_byte();
229:                 let end = node.end_byte().max(start + 1);
230:                 let pos = node.start_position();
231:                 diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
232:                     rule_id: "SYNER",
233:                     message: format!("Missing expected '{}'", node.kind()),
234:                     severity: Severity::Error,
235:                     byte_range: start..end,
236:                     line: pos.row + 1,
237:                     column: pos.column + 1,
238:                     fix: None,
239:                 });
240:             }
241:         }
242: 
243:         let mut cursor = node.walk();
244:         for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
245:             self.walk_error_nodes(child, source, last, diagnostics);
246:         }
247:     }

1: //! `check_file_name` — one check of the Syntax Errors engine.
2: 
3: use super::*;
4: 
5: impl SyntaxErrorsEngine {
6:     pub(crate) fn check_file_name(&self, ctx: &FileContext) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
7:         let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
8: 
9:         if !self.is_check_enabled("BDFIL") {
10:             return diagnostics;
11:         }
12: 
13:         if let Some(stem) = ctx.file_path.file_stem() {
14:             let name = stem.to_string_lossy();
15: 
16:             let valid = !name.is_empty()
17:                 && name.len() <= 63
18:                 && name.starts_with(|c: char| c.is_ascii_alphabetic())
19:                 && name.chars().all(|c| c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || c == '_');
20: 
21:             if !valid {
22:                 let reason = if name.is_empty() {
23:                     "file name is empty".to_string()
24:                 } else if name.len() > 63 {
25:                     format!("file name exceeds 63 characters ({} chars)", name.len())
26:                 } else if !name.starts_with(|c: char| c.is_ascii_alphabetic()) {
27:                     "file name must start with a letter".to_string()
28:                 } else {
29:                     "file name contains invalid characters (only alphanumeric and underscore allowed)".to_string()
30:                 };
31:                 diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
32:                     rule_id: "BDFIL",
33:                     message: format!("Invalid MATLAB file name '{}': {}", name, reason),
34:                     severity: Severity::Error,
35:                     byte_range: 0..ctx.source.len().min(1),
36:                     line: 1,
37:                     column: 1,
38:                     fix: None,
39:                 });
40:             }
41:         }
42: 
43:         diagnostics
44:     }
45: }

1: //! `check_number_literals` — one check of the Syntax Errors engine.
2: 
3: use super::*;
4: 
5: impl SyntaxErrorsEngine {
6:     pub(crate) fn check_number_literals(&self, root: Node, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
7:         let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
8:         let mut numbers = Vec::new();
9:         let mut errors = Vec::new();
10:         Self::collect_numbers_and_errors(root, &mut numbers, &mut errors);
11:         errors.sort_by_key(|node| node.start_byte());
12: 
13:         for number in numbers {
14:             let start = number.start_byte();
15:             let end = number.end_byte();
16:             let text = &source[start..end];
17: 
18:             // Truncated literal checks: an ERROR node immediately following
19:             // the number holds the invalid remainder of the literal.
20:             if !Self::inside_error(number) {
21:                 if let Ok(idx) = errors.binary_search_by_key(&end, |n| n.start_byte()) {
22:                     let err_text = &source[errors[idx].byte_range()];
23:                     if let Some(first) = err_text.chars().next() {
24:                         let literal_like = first.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || first == '_';
25:                         if (text.starts_with("0x") || text.starts_with("0X"))
26:                             && self.is_check_enabled("BADHBH")
27:                             && literal_like
28:                         {
29:                             diagnostics.push(Self::number_diagnostic(
30:                                     "BADHBH",
31:                                     "Invalid digit in hexadecimal literal. Supported hex digits are 0-9 and A-F. Supported type suffixes are u8,u16,u32,u64 and s8,s16,s32,s64.",
32:                                     number,
33:                                 ));
34:                         } else if (text.starts_with("0b") || text.starts_with("0B"))
35:                             && self.is_check_enabled("BADHBB")
36:                             && literal_like
37:                         {
38:                             diagnostics.push(Self::number_diagnostic(
39:                                     "BADHBB",
40:                                     "Invalid digit in binary literal. Supported binary digits are 0 and 1. Supported type suffixes are u8,u16,u32,u64 and s8,s16,s32,s64.",
41:                                     number,
42:                                 ));
43:                         } else if self.is_check_enabled("BADFP")
44:                             && (first == '.' || first.is_ascii_digit())
45:                         {
46:                             diagnostics.push(Self::number_diagnostic(
47:                                 "BADFP",
48:                                 "Invalid floating-point constant",
49:                                 number,
50:                             ));
51:                         }
52:                     }
53:                 }
54:             }
55: 
56:             // Digit-count checks for hex and binary literals.
57:             if let Some((is_hex, digit_count, suffix)) = Self::parse_hex_binary_literal(text) {
58:                 match suffix {
59:                     Some(suffix) => {
60:                         if let Some(max) = Self::max_digits_for_suffix(suffix, is_hex) {
61:                             if digit_count > max {
62:                                 let (rule_id, message) = if is_hex {
63:                                     (
64:                                             "BADHBHT",
65:                                             "Hexadecimal literal has too many digits for specified type suffix",
66:                                         )
67:                                 } else {
68:                                     (
69:                                             "BADHBBT",
70:                                             "Binary literal has too many digits for specified type suffix",
71:                                         )
72:                                 };
73:                                 if self.is_check_enabled(rule_id) {
74:                                     diagnostics
75:                                         .push(Self::number_diagnostic(rule_id, message, number));
76:                                 }
77:                             }
78:                         }
79:                     }
80:                     None => {
81:                         if is_hex && digit_count > 16 && self.is_check_enabled("HEXTOOLONG") {
82:                             diagnostics.push(Self::number_diagnostic(
83:                                 "HEXTOOLONG",
84:                                 "Hexadecimal literal has too many digits",
85:                                 number,
86:                             ));
87:                         } else if !is_hex
88:                             && digit_count > 64
89:                             && self.is_check_enabled("BINARYTOOLONG")
90:                         {
91:                             diagnostics.push(Self::number_diagnostic(
92:                                 "BINARYTOOLONG",
93:                                 "Binary literal has too many digits",
94:                                 number,
95:                             ));
96:                         }
97:                     }
98:                 }
99:             }
100:         }
101: 
102:         diagnostics
103:     }
104: }

1: //! `check_assignment_lhs` — one check of the Syntax Errors engine.
2: 
3: use super::*;
4: 
5: impl SyntaxErrorsEngine {
6:     pub(crate) fn check_assignment_lhs(&self, root: Node, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
7:         let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
8:         self.walk_assignment_lhs(root, source, &mut diagnostics);
9:         diagnostics
10:     }
11: 
12:     pub(crate) fn walk_assignment_lhs(
13:         &self,
14:         node: Node,
15:         source: &str,
16:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
17:     ) {
18:         const OPERATOR_LHS_KINDS: [&str; 5] = [
19:             "comparison_operator",
20:             "binary_operator",
21:             "boolean_operator",
22:             "unary_operator",
23:             "postfix_operator",
24:         ];
25: 
26:         let kind = node.kind();
27: 
28:         if kind == "assignment" {
29:             let lhs = node.child_by_field_name("left");
30:             if let Some(lhs) = lhs {
31:                 let pos = lhs.start_position();
32: 
33:                 // UNSET: operator expression on the left side of `=`.
34:                 if self.is_check_enabled("UNSET") && OPERATOR_LHS_KINDS.contains(&lhs.kind()) {
35:                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
36:                         rule_id: "UNSET",
37:                         message: "Invalid use of operator on the left side of an assignment"
38:                             .to_string(),
39:                         severity: Severity::Error,
40:                         byte_range: lhs.byte_range(),
41:                         line: pos.row + 1,
42:                         column: pos.column + 1,
43:                         fix: None,
44:                     });
45:                 }
46: 
47:                 // LHROW: multi-output LHS containing a row separator (`;`).
48:                 if self.is_check_enabled("LHROW") && lhs.kind() == "multioutput_variable" {
49:                     let lhs_text = &source[lhs.start_byte()..lhs.end_byte()];
50:                     if lhs_text.contains(';') {
51:                         diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
52:                             rule_id: "LHROW",
53:                             message:
54:                                 "The left side of an assignment cannot have multiple rows (';')"
55:                                     .to_string(),
56:                             severity: Severity::Error,
57:                             byte_range: lhs.byte_range(),
58:                             line: pos.row + 1,
59:                             column: pos.column + 1,
60:                             fix: None,
61:                         });
62:                     }
63:                 }
64:             }
65:         }
66: 
67:         // UNSET fallback: the parser may emit an ERROR node (text starting
68:         // with `=`) as the sibling of a statement-level operator expression
69:         // instead of an assignment node (e.g., `x == 5 = 3;`).
70:         if self.is_check_enabled("UNSET") && node.is_error() {
71:             if let Some(prev) = node.prev_sibling() {
72:                 if OPERATOR_LHS_KINDS.contains(&prev.kind()) {
73:                     let err_text = &source[node.start_byte()..node.end_byte()];
74:                     if err_text.trim_start().starts_with('=') {
75:                         let pos = prev.start_position();
76:                         diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
77:                             rule_id: "UNSET",
78:                             message: "Invalid use of operator on the left side of an assignment"
79:                                 .to_string(),
80:                             severity: Severity::Error,
81:                             byte_range: prev.byte_range(),
82:                             line: pos.row + 1,
83:                             column: pos.column + 1,
84:                             fix: None,
85:                         });
86:                     }
87:                 }
88:             }
89:         }
90: 
91:         let mut cursor = node.walk();
92:         for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
93:             self.walk_assignment_lhs(child, source, diagnostics);
94:         }
95:     }
96: }

1: //! `check_call_syntax` — one check of the Syntax Errors engine.
2: 
3: use super::*;
4: 
5: impl SyntaxErrorsEngine {
6:     pub(crate) fn check_call_syntax(&self, root: Node, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
7:         let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
8:         self.walk_call_syntax(root, source, &mut diagnostics);
9:         diagnostics
10:     }
11: 
12:     pub(crate) fn walk_call_syntax(
13:         &self,
14:         node: Node,
15:         source: &str,
16:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
17:     ) {
18:         if node.kind() == "function_call" {
19:             self.check_function_call(node, source, diagnostics);
20:         }
21:         let mut cursor = node.walk();
22:         for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
23:             self.walk_call_syntax(child, source, diagnostics);
24:         }
25:     }
26: 
27:     pub(crate) fn check_function_call(
28:         &self,
29:         node: Node,
30:         source: &str,
31:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
32:     ) {
33:         // SBTMP: chaining outputs after parenthesis is not supported.
34:         if self.is_check_enabled("SBTMP") {
35:             if let Some(name) = node.child_by_field_name("name") {
36:                 if name.kind() == "function_call" {
37:                     let pos = node.start_position();
38:                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
39:                             rule_id: "SBTMP",
40:                             message: "Invalid array indexing or function call. Chaining outputs after parenthesis is not supported."
41:                                 .to_string(),
42:                             severity: Severity::Error,
43:                             byte_range: node.byte_range(),
44:                             line: pos.row + 1,
45:                             column: pos.column + 1,
46:                             fix: None,
47:                         });
48:                 }
49:             }
50:         }
51: 
52:         let is_brace =
53:             (0..node.child_count()).any(|i| node.child(i).is_some_and(|c| c.kind() == "{"));
54:         let args = Self::arguments_child(node);
55: 
56:         // FVACI: name=value syntax in cell indexing (`{}` calls).
57:         if self.is_check_enabled("FVACI") && is_brace {
58:             if let Some(a) = args {
59:                 if Self::has_eq_token(a) {
60:                     let pos = node.start_position();
61:                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
62:                         rule_id: "FVACI",
63:                         message: "Use of name-value arguments in cell indexing is not supported."
64:                             .to_string(),
65:                         severity: Severity::Error,
66:                         byte_range: node.byte_range(),
67:                         line: pos.row + 1,
68:                         column: pos.column + 1,
69:                         fix: None,
70:                     });
71:                 }
72:             }
73:         }
74: 
75:         // FVACS/FVAMI: name=value with an invalid name in a call.
76:         if self.is_check_enabled("FVACS") || self.is_check_enabled("FVAMI") {
77:             self.check_name_value(node, args, source, diagnostics);
78:         }
79:     }
80: }

1: //! `check_directional_formatting` — one check of the Syntax Errors engine.
2: 
3: use super::*;
4: 
5: impl SyntaxErrorsEngine {
6:     pub(crate) fn check_directional_formatting(&self, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
7:         if !self.is_check_enabled("BADCT") {
8:             return Vec::new();
9:         }
10: 
11:         let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
12:         let mut line = 1usize;
13:         let mut line_start = 0usize;
14: 
15:         for (i, ch) in source.char_indices() {
16:             if ch == '\n' {
17:                 line += 1;
18:                 line_start = i + 1;
19:                 continue;
20:             }
21:             let cp = ch as u32;
22:             // U+202A..U+202E (LRE, RLE, PDF, LRO, RLO) and
23:             // U+2066..U+2069 (LRI, RLI, FSI, PDI) are directional formatting
24:             // characters that MATLAB rejects.
25:             if (0x202A..=0x202E).contains(&cp) || (0x2066..=0x2069).contains(&cp) {
26:                 diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
27:                     rule_id: "BADCT",
28:                     message:
29:                         "Unicode explicit directional formatting characters are not supported."
30:                             .to_string(),
31:                     severity: Severity::Error,
32:                     byte_range: i..i + ch.len_utf8(),
33:                     line,
34:                     column: i - line_start + 1,
35:                     fix: None,
36:                 });
37:             }
38:         }
39: 
40:         diagnostics
41:     }
42: }
43:

1: //! `check_file` — one check of the Syntax Errors engine.
2: 
3: use super::*;
4: 
5: impl SyntaxErrorsEngine {
6:     pub(crate) fn scan_source_text(
7:         &self,
8:         source: &str,
9:         skip_ranges: &[Range<usize>],
10:     ) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
11:         let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
12:         let bytes = source.as_bytes();
13:         let len = bytes.len();
14: 
15:         // Track line/column for diagnostics.
16:         let mut line = 1usize;
17:         let mut line_start = 0usize;
18: 
19:         let mut i = 0;
20:         while i < len {
21:             let b = bytes[i];
22: 
23:             // Track newlines.
24:             if b == b'\n' {
25:                 line += 1;
26:                 line_start = i + 1;
27:                 i += 1;
28:                 continue;
29:             }
30: 
31:             // BADCH: Invalid control characters (< 0x20 except \t, \n, \r).
32:             if self.is_check_enabled("BADCH")
33:                 && b < 0x20
34:                 && b != b'\t'
35:                 && b != b'\n'
36:                 && b != b'\r'
37:                 && !Self::in_skip_range(i, skip_ranges)
38:             {
39:                 diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
40:                     rule_id: "BADCH",
41:                     message: format!("Invalid control character (0x{:02X}) in source", b),
42:                     severity: Severity::Error,
43:                     byte_range: i..i + 1,
44:                     line,
45:                     column: i - line_start + 1,
46:                     fix: None,
47:                 });
48:                 i += 1;
49:                 continue;
50:             }
51: 
52:             // BADSP: Non-ASCII whitespace detection.
53:             // Check for multi-byte UTF-8 sequences that are whitespace.
54:             if self.is_check_enabled("BADSP") && b > 0x7F && !Self::in_skip_range(i, skip_ranges) {
55:                 // Decode the UTF-8 character at this position.
56:                 if let Some(ch) = source[i..].chars().next() {
57:                     if ch.is_whitespace() && ch != ' ' && ch != '\t' && ch != '\n' && ch != '\r' {
58:                         let ch_len = ch.len_utf8();
59:                         diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
60:                             rule_id: "BADSP",
61:                             message: format!(
62:                                 "Non-ASCII whitespace character (U+{:04X}) in source",
63:                                 ch as u32
64:                             ),
65:                             severity: Severity::Error,
66:                             byte_range: i..i + ch_len,
67:                             line,
68:                             column: i - line_start + 1,
69:                             fix: None,
70:                         });
71:                         i += ch_len;
72:                         continue;
73:                     }
74:                 }
75:             }
76: 
77:             // BADNE: `!=` (MATLAB uses `~=`).
78:             if self.is_check_enabled("BADNE")
79:                 && b == b'!'
80:                 && i + 1 < len
81:                 && bytes[i + 1] == b'='
82:                 && !Self::in_skip_range(i, skip_ranges)
83:             {
84:                 diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
85:                     rule_id: "BADNE",
86:                     message: "Use '~=' instead of '!=' for not-equal in MATLAB".to_string(),
87:                     severity: Severity::Error,
88:                     byte_range: i..i + 2,
89:                     line,
90:                     column: i - line_start + 1,
91:                     fix: Some(mlt_core::Fix::new(i..i + 2, "~=")),
92:                 });
93:                 i += 2;
94:                 continue;
95:             }
96: 
97:             // BADOT: `..` not part of `...` (line continuation).
98:             if self.is_check_enabled("BADOT")
99:                 && b == b'.'
100:                 && i + 1 < len
101:                 && bytes[i + 1] == b'.'
102:                 && !Self::in_skip_range(i, skip_ranges)
103:             {
104:                 // Check if this is part of `...` (line continuation).
105:                 let is_ellipsis = i + 2 < len && bytes[i + 2] == b'.';
106:                 if !is_ellipsis {
107:                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
108:                         rule_id: "BADOT",
109:                         message: "Invalid '..' operator; did you mean '...' (line continuation)?"
110:                             .to_string(),
111:                         severity: Severity::Error,
112:                         byte_range: i..i + 2,
113:                         line,
114:                         column: i - line_start + 1,
115:                         fix: None,
116:                     });
117:                     i += 2;
118:                     continue;
119:                 } else {
120:                     // Skip the whole `...`.
121:                     i += 3;
122:                     continue;
123:                 }
124:             }
125: 
126:             // TWOCM: `,,` (double comma).
127:             if self.is_check_enabled("TWOCM")
128:                 && b == b','
129:                 && i + 1 < len
130:                 && bytes[i + 1] == b','
131:                 && !Self::in_skip_range(i, skip_ranges)
132:             {
133:                 diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
134:                     rule_id: "TWOCM",
135:                     message: "Double comma ',,'; possible typo".to_string(),
136:                     severity: Severity::Error,
137:                     byte_range: i..i + 2,
138:                     line,
139:                     column: i - line_start + 1,
140:                     fix: None,
141:                 });
142:                 i += 2;
143:                 continue;
144:             }
145: 
146:             // Advance past multi-byte UTF-8 characters.
147:             if b > 0x7F {
148:                 if let Some(ch) = source[i..].chars().next() {
149:                     i += ch.len_utf8();
150:                     continue;
151:                 }
152:             }
153: 
154:             i += 1;
155:         }
156: 
157:         diagnostics
158:     }
159: }

1: //! `check_file_structure` — one check of the Syntax Errors engine.
2: 
3: use super::*;
4: 
5: impl SyntaxErrorsEngine {
6:     pub(crate) fn check_file_structure(&self, root: Node, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
7:         let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
8:         let mut cursor = root.walk();
9: 
10:         let mut class_count = 0usize;
11:         let mut has_non_class_statements = false;
12:         let mut has_function_def = false;
13:         let mut has_any_real_content = false;
14: 
15:         for child in root.children(&mut cursor) {
16:             let kind = child.kind();
17:             match kind {
18:                 "class_definition" => class_count += 1,
19:                 "function_definition" => {
20:                     has_function_def = true;
21:                     has_any_real_content = true;
22:                 }
23:                 "comment" => {} // Comments don't count as content.
24:                 "expression_statement" => {
25:                     // Check if it's just a semicolon.
26:                     let text = &source[child.start_byte()..child.end_byte()];
27:                     let trimmed = text.trim();
28:                     if trimmed == ";" {
29:                         // Empty statement — doesn't count as real content.
30:                     } else {
31:                         has_non_class_statements = true;
32:                         has_any_real_content = true;
33:                     }
34:                 }
35:                 _ if !child.is_error() && kind != "\n" => {
36:                     has_non_class_statements = true;
37:                     has_any_real_content = true;
38:                 }
39:                 _ => {}
40:             }
41:         }
42: 
43:         // CLTWO: Multiple class definitions in one file.
44:         if self.is_check_enabled("CLTWO") && class_count > 1 {
45:             diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
46:                 rule_id: "CLTWO",
47:                 message: format!(
48:                     "File contains {class_count} class definitions; only one is allowed per file"
49:                 ),
50:                 severity: Severity::Error,
51:                 byte_range: 0..source.len().min(1),
52:                 line: 1,
53:                 column: 1,
54:                 fix: None,
55:             });
56:         }
57: 
58:         // CLIS: Class definition in a script file (non-function statements exist).
59:         if self.is_check_enabled("CLIS")
60:             && class_count > 0
61:             && has_non_class_statements
62:             && !has_function_def
63:         {
64:             diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
65:                 rule_id: "CLIS",
66:                 message: "Class definition in a script file; statements exist outside the class"
67:                     .to_string(),
68:                 severity: Severity::Error,
69:                 byte_range: 0..source.len().min(1),
70:                 line: 1,
71:                 column: 1,
72:                 fix: None,
73:             });
74:         }
75: 
76:         // SOFOC: Statements outside a class definition in a class file.
77:         if self.is_check_enabled("SOFOC")
78:             && class_count > 0
79:             && has_non_class_statements
80:             && has_function_def
81:         {
82:             diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
83:                 rule_id: "SOFOC",
84:                 message: "Statements outside class definition in a class file are not allowed"
85:                     .to_string(),
86:                 severity: Severity::Error,
87:                 byte_range: 0..source.len().min(1),
88:                 line: 1,
89:                 column: 1,
90:                 fix: None,
91:             });
92:         }
93: 
94:         // SEMFU: File has only empty statements (only `;` and whitespace).
95:         if self.is_check_enabled("SEMFU")
96:             && !has_any_real_content
97:             && class_count == 0
98:             && !source.trim().is_empty()
99:         {
100:             // Verify the file truly only has semicolons, whitespace, and comments.
101:             let only_empty = source.lines().all(|line| {
102:                 let trimmed = line.trim();
103:                 trimmed.is_empty() || trimmed == ";" || trimmed.starts_with('%')
104:             });
105:             if only_empty {
106:                 diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
107:                     rule_id: "SEMFU",
108:                     message: "File contains only empty statements (semicolons and whitespace)"
109:                         .to_string(),
110:                     severity: Severity::Error,
111:                     byte_range: 0..source.len().min(1),
112:                     line: 1,
113:                     column: 1,
114:                     fix: None,
115:                 });
116:             }
117:         }
118: 
119:         diagnostics
120:     }
121: }

13:         &self,
14:         node: Node,
15:         source: &str,
16:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
17:         in_methods_block: bool,
18:     ) {
19:         let kind = node.kind();
20:         let is_methods = kind == "methods";
21: 
22:         if kind == "function_definition" {
23:             // Find the function name node.
24:             if let Some(name_node) = node.child_by_field_name("name") {
25:                 let name = &source[name_node.start_byte()..name_node.end_byte()];
26:                 let pos = name_node.start_position();
27: 
28:                 // FNSWA: Function name doesn't start with alphabetic character.
29:                 if self.is_check_enabled("FNSWA")
30:                     && !name.starts_with(|c: char| c.is_ascii_alphabetic())
31:                 {
32:                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
33:                         rule_id: "FNSWA",
34:                         message: format!(
35:                             "Function name '{}' must start with an alphabetic character",
36:                             name
37:                         ),
38:                         severity: Severity::Error,
39:                         byte_range: name_node.byte_range(),
40:                         line: pos.row + 1,
41:                         column: pos.column + 1,
42:                         fix: None,
43:                     });
44:                 }
45: 
46:                 // FNDOT: Function name contains dots but is not in a class methods block.
47:                 if self.is_check_enabled("FNDOT") && name.contains('.') && !in_methods_block {
48:                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
49:                         rule_id: "FNDOT",
50:                         message: format!(
51:                             "Function name '{}' contains dots but is not in a class methods block",
52:                             name
53:                         ),
54:                         severity: Severity::Error,
55:                         byte_range: name_node.byte_range(),
56:                         line: pos.row + 1,
57:                         column: pos.column + 1,
58:                         fix: None,
59:                     });
60:                 }
61:             }
62:         }
63: 
64:         let mut cursor = node.walk();
65:         for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
66:             self.walk_function_names(child, source, diagnostics, in_methods_block || is_methods);
67:         }
68:     }
69: }

1: //! `check_name_value` — one check of the Syntax Errors engine.
2: 
3: use super::*;
4: 
5: impl SyntaxErrorsEngine {
6:     pub(crate) fn check_name_value(
7:         &self,
8:         call: Node,
9:         args: Option<Node>,
10:         source: &str,
11:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
12:     ) {
13:         // Assignment shape: `f('Bad Name' = 1)` parses as an assignment whose
14:         // LHS is a function_call with a MISSING closing paren.
15:         let is_assignment_lhs = call.parent().is_some_and(|p| {
16:             p.kind() == "assignment"
17:                 && p.child_by_field_name("left")
18:                     .is_some_and(|l| l.id() == call.id())
19:         });
20:         let has_missing_paren = (0..call.child_count()).any(|i| {
21:             call.child(i)
22:                 .is_some_and(|c| c.is_missing() && c.kind() == ")")
23:         });
24:         if is_assignment_lhs && has_missing_paren {
25:             if let Some(name) = args.and_then(Self::last_named_child) {
26:                 self.push_name_value_diagnostic(name, source, diagnostics);
27:             }
28:         }
29: 
30:         // ERROR shape: an ERROR node containing `=` inside the call's args.
31:         for e in Self::call_error_nodes(call) {
32:             let text = &source[e.start_byte()..e.end_byte()];
33:             if !text.contains('=') {
34:                 continue;
35:             }
36:             let name = if Self::has_string_child(e) {
37:                 e
38:             } else if let Some(last) = args.and_then(Self::last_named_child) {
39:                 last
40:             } else {
41:                 e
42:             };
43:             self.push_name_value_diagnostic(name, source, diagnostics);
44:         }
45: 
46:         // Direct `=` tokens inside arguments (name=value parses cleanly only
47:         // for valid identifier names).
48:         if let Some(a) = args {
49:             for i in 0..a.child_count() {
50:                 if let Some(eq) = a.child(i) {
51:                     if eq.kind() != "=" {
52:                         continue;
53:                     }
54:                     if let Some(name) = eq.prev_named_sibling() {
55:                         self.push_name_value_diagnostic(name, source, diagnostics);
56:                     }
57:                 }
58:             }
59:         }
60:     }
61: }
