1: //! `check_reserved_and_not` — one check of the Syntax Errors engine.
2: 
3: use super::*;
4: 
5: impl SyntaxErrorsEngine {
6:     pub(crate) fn check_reserved_and_not(&self, root: Node, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
7:         let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
8:         self.walk_reserved_and_not(root, source, &mut diagnostics);
9:         diagnostics
10:     }
11: 
12:     pub(crate) fn walk_reserved_and_not(
13:         &self,
14:         node: Node,
15:         source: &str,
16:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
17:     ) {
18:         let kind = node.kind();
19: 
20:         if node.is_error() {
21:             let start = node.start_byte();
22:             let end = node.end_byte().max(start + 1);
23:             let pos = node.start_position();
24:             let text = &source[start..end.min(source.len())];
25: 
26:             // MCPLD: ERROR inside a property declaration in a properties block.
27:             if self.is_check_enabled("MCPLD") && Self::inside_property(node) {
28:                 let name = Self::ancestor_of_kind(node, "property")
29:                     .and_then(|prop| Self::first_child_text(prop, "identifier", source))
30:                     .unwrap_or("(unknown)");
31:                 diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
32:                     rule_id: "MCPLD",
33:                     message: format!("Invalid property syntax at {name}"),
34:                     severity: Severity::Error,
35:                     byte_range: start..end,
36:                     line: pos.row + 1,
37:                     column: pos.column + 1,
38:                     fix: None,
39:                 });
40:             }
41: 
42:             // SYNEND takes priority over RESWD for `end`.
43:             if self.is_check_enabled("SYNEND") && Self::has_descendant_kind(node, "end_keyword") {
44:                 diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
45:                     rule_id: "SYNEND",
46:                     message: "Invalid use for END operator".to_string(),
47:                     severity: Severity::Error,
48:                     byte_range: start..end,
49:                     line: pos.row + 1,
50:                     column: pos.column + 1,
51:                     fix: None,
52:                 });
53:             } else if self.is_check_enabled("RESWD") {
54:                 if let Some(kw) = Self::contains_reserved_word(text) {
55:                     if kw != "end" {
56:                         diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
57:                             rule_id: "RESWD",
58:                             message: "Invalid use of a reserved word.".to_string(),
59:                             severity: Severity::Error,
60:                             byte_range: start..end,
61:                             line: pos.row + 1,
62:                             column: pos.column + 1,
63:                             fix: None,
64:                         });
65:                     }
66:                 }
67:             }
68: 
69:             // BADNOT: bare `~` statement.
70:             if self.is_check_enabled("BADNOT") && text.trim() == "~" {
71:                 diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
72:                     rule_id: "BADNOT",
73:                     message: "Using ~ to ignore a value is not permitted in this context."
74:                         .to_string(),
75:                     severity: Severity::Error,
76:                     byte_range: start..end,
77:                     line: pos.row + 1,
78:                     column: pos.column + 1,
79:                     fix: None,
80:                 });
81:             }
82:         }
83: 
84:         // BADNOT: `~` used as a value operator with a malformed operand.
85:         if kind == "not_operator"
86:             && self.is_check_enabled("BADNOT")
87:             && Self::has_error_or_missing_descendant(node)
88:         {
89:             let start = node.start_byte();
90:             let end = node.end_byte();
91:             let pos = node.start_position();
92:             diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
93:                 rule_id: "BADNOT",
94:                 message: "Using ~ to ignore a value is not permitted in this context.".to_string(),
95:                 severity: Severity::Error,
96:                 byte_range: start..end,
97:                 line: pos.row + 1,
98:                 column: pos.column + 1,
99:                 fix: None,
100:             });
101:         }
102: 
103:         // BADNOTLHS: `~` adjacent to an output variable without a comma.
104:         if kind == "multioutput_variable" && self.is_check_enabled("BADNOTLHS") {
105:             let mut cursor = node.walk();
106:             let children: Vec<Node> = node.children(&mut cursor).collect();
107:             for (i, child) in children.iter().enumerate() {
108:                 if child.kind() != "ignored_argument" {
109:                     continue;
110:                 }
111:                 let prev_is_id = i > 0 && children[i - 1].kind() == "identifier";
112:                 let next_is_id = i + 1 < children.len() && children[i + 1].kind() == "identifier";
113:                 if prev_is_id || next_is_id {
114:                     let pos = child.start_position();
115:                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
116:                             rule_id: "BADNOTLHS",
117:                             message: "Invalid use of logical not operator (~) on left side of an assignment. To use ~ to ignore function outputs, separate output variables with commas."
118:                                 .to_string(),
119:                             severity: Severity::Error,
120:                             byte_range: child.byte_range(),
121:                             line: pos.row + 1,
122:                             column: pos.column + 1,
123:                             fix: None,
124:                         });
125:                 }
126:             }
127:         }
128: 
129:         let mut cursor = node.walk();
130:         for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
131:             self.walk_reserved_and_not(child, source, diagnostics);
132:         }
133:     }
134: }

1: //! `check_statements` — one check of the Syntax Errors engine.
2: 
3: use super::*;
4: 
5: impl SyntaxErrorsEngine {
6:     pub(crate) fn check_statements(&self, root: Node, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
7:         let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
8: 
9:         // Collect function names and variable assignments for REDEF.
10:         let mut function_names: HashSet<String> = HashSet::new();
11:         let mut variable_names: HashSet<String> = HashSet::new();
12:         let mut redef_reported: HashSet<String> = HashSet::new();
13: 
14:         self.walk_statements(
15:             root,
16:             source,
17:             &mut diagnostics,
18:             &mut function_names,
19:             &mut variable_names,
20:             &mut redef_reported,
21:         );
22: 
23:         diagnostics
24:     }
25: 
26:     pub(crate) fn walk_statements(
27:         &self,
28:         node: Node,
29:         source: &str,
30:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
31:         function_names: &mut HashSet<String>,
32:         variable_names: &mut HashSet<String>,
33:         redef_reported: &mut HashSet<String>,
34:     ) {
35:         let kind = node.kind();
36: 
37:         // NOLHS: Assignment with empty left side.
38:         if self.is_check_enabled("NOLHS") && kind == "assignment" {
39:             if let Some(lhs) = node.child_by_field_name("left") {
40:                 let lhs_text = &source[lhs.start_byte()..lhs.end_byte()];
41:                 if lhs_text.trim().is_empty() {
42:                     let pos = node.start_position();
43:                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
44:                         rule_id: "NOLHS",
45:                         message: "Assignment with empty left-hand side".to_string(),
46:                         severity: Severity::Error,
47:                         byte_range: node.byte_range(),
48:                         line: pos.row + 1,
49:                         column: pos.column + 1,
50:                         fix: None,
51:                     });
52:                 }
53:             }
54:         }
55: 
56:         // REDEF: Track function definitions and variable assignments.
57:         if kind == "function_definition" {
58:             if let Some(name_node) = node.child_by_field_name("name") {
59:                 let name = source[name_node.start_byte()..name_node.end_byte()].to_string();
60:                 if self.is_check_enabled("REDEF")
61:                     && variable_names.contains(&name)
62:                     && !redef_reported.contains(&name)
63:                 {
64:                     let pos = name_node.start_position();
65:                     diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
66:                         rule_id: "REDEF",
67:                         message: format!(
68:                             "Identifier '{}' is used as both a function name and a variable",
69:                             name
70:                         ),
71:                         severity: Severity::Error,
72:                         byte_range: name_node.byte_range(),
73:                         line: pos.row + 1,
74:                         column: pos.column + 1,
75:                         fix: None,
76:                     });
77:                     redef_reported.insert(name.clone());
78:                 }
79:                 function_names.insert(name);
80:             }
81:         }
82: 
83:         if kind == "assignment" {
84:             if let Some(lhs) = node.child_by_field_name("left") {
85:                 let lhs_kind = lhs.kind();
86:                 if lhs_kind == "identifier" {
87:                     let name = source[lhs.start_byte()..lhs.end_byte()].to_string();
88:                     if self.is_check_enabled("REDEF")
89:                         && function_names.contains(&name)
90:                         && !redef_reported.contains(&name)
91:                     {
92:                         let pos = lhs.start_position();
93:                         diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
94:                             rule_id: "REDEF",
95:                             message: format!(
96:                                 "Identifier '{}' is used as both a function name and a variable",
97:                                 name
98:                             ),
99:                             severity: Severity::Error,
100:                             byte_range: lhs.byte_range(),
101:                             line: pos.row + 1,
102:                             column: pos.column + 1,
103:                             fix: None,
104:                         });
105:                         redef_reported.insert(name.clone());
106:                     }
107:                     variable_names.insert(name);
108:                 }
109:             }
110:         }
111: 
112:         // SEPEXR: Missing separator between statements.
113:         // Check consecutive children of block/source_file that are statements
114:         // on the same line without separator.
115:         if self.is_check_enabled("SEPEXR") && (kind == "source_file" || kind == "block") {
116:             let mut cursor = node.walk();
117:             let children: Vec<Node> = node.children(&mut cursor).collect();
118: 
119:             for pair in children.windows(2) {
120:                 let prev = pair[0];
121:                 let curr = pair[1];
122: 
123:                 // Skip error nodes and comments.
124:                 if prev.is_error() || curr.is_error() {
125:                     continue;
126:                 }
127:                 if prev.kind() == "comment" || curr.kind() == "comment" {
128:                     continue;
129:                 }
130: 
131:                 // Check if they're on the same line with no separator.
132:                 let prev_end = prev.end_position();
133:                 let curr_start = curr.start_position();
134: 
135:                 if prev_end.row == curr_start.row {
136:                     // Check the text between them for a separator (; or ,).
137:                     let between_start = prev.end_byte();
138:                     let between_end = curr.start_byte();
139:                     if between_start < between_end {
140:                         let between = &source[between_start..between_end];
141:                         let has_separator = between.contains(';') || between.contains(',');
142:                         if !has_separator {
143:                             let pos = curr.start_position();
144:                             diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
145:                                 rule_id: "SEPEXR",
146:                                 message: "Missing semicolon or newline between statements"
147:                                     .to_string(),
148:                                 severity: Severity::Error,
149:                                 byte_range: curr.byte_range(),
150:                                 line: pos.row + 1,
151:                                 column: pos.column + 1,
152:                                 fix: Some(mlt_core::Fix::insert(between_start, ";")),
153:                             });
154:                         }
155:                     }
156:                 }
157:             }
158:         }
159: 
160:         // Recurse into children.
161:         let mut cursor = node.walk();
162:         for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
163:             self.walk_statements(
164:                 child,
165:                 source,
166:                 diagnostics,
167:                 function_names,
168:                 variable_names,
169:                 redef_reported,
170:             );
171:         }

1: //! `check_unterminated` — one check of the Syntax Errors engine.
2: 
3: use super::*;
4: 
5: impl SyntaxErrorsEngine {
6:     pub(crate) fn check_unterminated(&self, root: Node, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
7:         let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
8:         let mut reported: HashSet<usize> = HashSet::new();
9: 
10:         if self.is_check_enabled("STRIN") || self.is_check_enabled("DOUQT") {
11:             Self::walk_unterminated_strings(root, source, &mut diagnostics, &mut reported);
12:         }
13: 
14:         if self.is_check_enabled("INBLK") {
15:             Self::walk_unterminated_comments(root, source, &mut diagnostics);
16:         }
17: 
18:         diagnostics
19:     }
20: 
21:     pub(crate) fn walk_unterminated_strings(
22:         node: Node,
23:         source: &str,
24:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
25:         reported: &mut HashSet<usize>,
26:     ) {
27:         if node.is_error() {
28:             // STRIN: ERROR node whose text starts with an unmatched quote.
29:             let start = node.start_byte();
30:             let end = node.end_byte().min(source.len());
31:             let text = &source[start..end];
32:             if text.starts_with('\'')
33:                 && text.matches('\'').count() % 2 == 1
34:                 && !reported.contains(&start)
35:                 && !Self::is_transpose_position(source, start)
36:             {
37:                 let pos = node.start_position();
38:                 reported.insert(start);
39:                 diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
40:                     rule_id: "STRIN",
41:                     message: "A quoted character vector is unterminated.".to_string(),
42:                     severity: Severity::Error,
43:                     byte_range: start..start + 1,
44:                     line: pos.row + 1,
45:                     column: pos.column + 1,
46:                     fix: None,
47:                 });
48:             }
49: 
50:             // STRIN/DOUQT: direct quote tokens inside the ERROR node.
51:             let mut cursor = node.walk();
52:             for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
53:                 if child.kind() == "'" {
54:                     let pos = child.start_byte();
55:                     if !reported.contains(&pos) && !Self::is_transpose_position(source, pos) {
56:                         let cpos = child.start_position();
57:                         reported.insert(pos);
58:                         diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
59:                             rule_id: "STRIN",
60:                             message: "A quoted character vector is unterminated.".to_string(),
61:                             severity: Severity::Error,
62:                             byte_range: pos..pos + 1,
63:                             line: cpos.row + 1,
64:                             column: cpos.column + 1,
65:                             fix: None,
66:                         });
67:                     }
68:                 } else if child.kind() == "\"" {
69:                     let pos = child.start_byte();
70:                     if !reported.contains(&pos) {
71:                         let cpos = child.start_position();
72:                         reported.insert(pos);
73:                         diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
74:                             rule_id: "DOUQT",
75:                             message: "A double quoted string is unterminated.".to_string(),
76:                             severity: Severity::Error,
77:                             byte_range: pos..pos + 1,
78:                             line: cpos.row + 1,
79:                             column: cpos.column + 1,
80:                             fix: None,
81:                         });
82:                     }
83:                 }
84:             }
85:         }
86: 
87:         let mut cursor = node.walk();
88:         for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
89:             Self::walk_unterminated_strings(child, source, diagnostics, reported);
90:         }
91:     }
92: 
93:     pub(crate) fn walk_unterminated_comments(
94:         node: Node,
95:         source: &str,
96:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
97:     ) {
98:         if node.kind() == "comment" {
99:             let text = &source[node.start_byte()..node.end_byte()];
100:             if text.starts_with("%{") && !text.contains("%}") {
101:                 let pos = node.start_position();
102:                 diagnostics.push(Diagnostic {
103:                     rule_id: "INBLK",
104:                     message: "A block comment is unterminated at the end of the file.".to_string(),
105:                     severity: Severity::Error,
106:                     byte_range: node.byte_range(),
107:                     line: pos.row + 1,
108:                     column: pos.column + 1,
109:                     fix: None,
110:                 });
111:             }
112:             return;
113:         }
114:         let mut cursor = node.walk();
115:         for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
116:             Self::walk_unterminated_comments(child, source, diagnostics);
117:         }
118:     }
119: }

1: //! `check_validation_order` — one check of the Syntax Errors engine.
2: 
3: use super::*;
4: 
5: impl SyntaxErrorsEngine {
6:     pub(crate) fn check_validation_order(&self, root: Node, source: &str) -> Vec<Diagnostic> {
7:         let mut diagnostics = Vec::new();
8:         if !self.is_check_enabled("VTPOD") {
9:             return diagnostics;
10:         }
11:         self.walk_validation_order(root, source, &mut diagnostics);
12:         diagnostics
13:     }
14: 
15:     pub(crate) fn walk_validation_order(
16:         &self,
17:         node: Node,
18:         source: &str,
19:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
20:     ) {
21:         if node.kind() == "arguments_statement" {
22:             let mut cursor = node.walk();
23:             for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
24:                 if child.kind() == "property" {
25:                     self.check_property_validation_order(child, source, diagnostics);
26:                 }
27:             }
28:         }
29:         let mut cursor = node.walk();
30:         for child in node.children(&mut cursor) {
31:             self.walk_validation_order(child, source, diagnostics);
32:         }
33:     }
34: 
35:     pub(crate) fn check_property_validation_order(
36:         &self,
37:         property: Node,
38:         source: &str,
39:         diagnostics: &mut Vec<Diagnostic>,
40:     ) {
41:         let name = property.child_by_field_name("name");
42:         let vf = Self::find_validation_functions(property);
43:         let mut class_id: Option<Node> = None;
44: 
45:         for i in 0..property.child_count() {
46:             let Some(child) = property.child(i) else {
47:                 continue;
48:             };
49:             if child.kind() == "identifier" && Some(child) != name && class_id.is_none() {
50:                 class_id = Some(child);
51:             }
52:         }
53: 
54:         // Pattern A: a class identifier appears after the validation functions.
55:         if let (Some(class_id), Some(vf)) = (class_id, vf) {
56:             if class_id.start_byte() > vf.start_byte() {
57:                 self.push_vtpod(class_id, diagnostics);
58:                 return;
59:             }
60:         }
61: 
62:         // Pattern B: a class name appears inside the validation functions.
63:         if class_id.is_none() {
64:             if let Some(vf) = vf {
65:                 let mut cursor = vf.walk();
66:                 for child in vf.children(&mut cursor) {
67:                     if child.kind() != "identifier" {
68:                         continue;
69:                     }
70:                     let text = &source[child.start_byte()..child.end_byte()];
71:                     if KNOWN_CLASS_NAMES.contains(&text) {
72:                         self.push_vtpod(child, diagnostics);
73:                     }
74:                 }
75:             }
76:         }
77:     }
78: }
